identityModel.connectionId: chconn-<sha256(sourceNamespace, platform.provider, platform.deployment, accountId, nativeAccountId, accountKind)[:32]>
identityModel.conversationRef: chconv-<sha256(connectionId, nativeConversationId, threadId|null, audienceMode)[:32]>; audienceMode is part of the identity so DM/group/thread never merge
identityModel.participantRef: chpart-<sha256(sourceNamespace, accountId, nativeParticipantId)[:32]>; display names, aliases, roles and body text never participate; cross-account same short id stays distinct
identityModel.sourceEventId: explicit nativeEventId, otherwise composed as nativeMessageId#r<revision>#<kind>; dedupe key adds sourceNamespace+accountId+resource(conversationRef)
identityModel.trustBoundary: identity/routing fields are a strict validated envelope supplied by the registered trusted adapter; content (digest, opaque bodyRef, bounded summary, attachment refs) is data and cannot add envelope fields, roles or scopes; an explicit native event id reused under another conversation label is refused as SOURCE_EVENT_CONFLICT
identityModel.crossDomain: toInnerAccount() validates against the H4 InnerAccount contract (identityNamespace = <sourceNamespace>:<accountId>, externalSubjectId = nativeParticipantId, identityType = channel-<kind>); toConversationKey() maps the channel audience to the existing ConversationStore key shape

dedupeModel.key: (sourceNamespace, accountId, conversationRef, sourceEventId) persisted unique; payload fingerprint over the validated envelope without the dedupe id
dedupeModel.duplicate: same key + same fingerprint returns the stored receipt (accepted becomes duplicate) with the original intakeSeq and identity; no row is written
dedupeModel.conflict: same key + different fingerprint is persisted as an intake conflict and returned as rejected IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; replayed conflicts keep the same intake sequence
dedupeModel.crossChannel: explicit native event ids are unique per account; reuse under another conversation is rejected SOURCE_EVENT_CONFLICT, composed ids remain conversation scoped
dedupeModel.ordering: native message revision gates edits/retract/delete (strictly greater applies; equal/lower is a persisted stale receipt); trusted per-conversation sequence is recorded as evidence, received order is never rewritten
dedupeModel.batch: one SQLite transaction per ingest batch; a malformed envelope rejects the whole batch, business rejections return per-event receipts, defensive limits fail without partial writes

revisionModel.state: messages keep status active|edited|retracted|deleted, our monotonic revision count, native revision, last event kind and first/last intake sequence
revisionModel.provenance: every accepted revision row keeps kind, sourceEventId, native revision, participant, privacy class, content hash/bodyRef/summary/attachment refs and source sequence; terminal revisions keep kind/source/native revision but no content references
revisionModel.terminal: retract and delete are terminal tombstones: content references (message row, every revision row) are cleared, the digest/provenance stays, a deletion watermark and typed invalidation are appended, later edit/delete/create cannot resurrect
revisionModel.stale: a late lower native revision is recorded as stale and cannot overwrite the current content; old revision references remain provenance only

audienceModel.direct: exactly one counterpart participant for the conversation lifetime; a different or additional counterpart fails AUDIENCE_MODE_CONFLICT, explicit revokeAccess is required
audienceModel.groupChannel: replaceable member set with a monotonic audienceVersion; order-insensitive equality is idempotent; removals append participant revocations (one revocation watermark each) and an audience_changed invalidation in the same transaction
audienceModel.cas: every audience mutation takes expectedAudienceVersion and fails VERSION_CONFLICT on a stale reader
audienceModel.revocation: revokeAccess(scope participant|conversation) bumps the audience version, appends a revocation row/watermark and a typed invalidation; revoked participants cannot be re-added and a revoked conversation refuses capture and new intake
audienceModel.invalidationSignal: a synchronous same-Worker sink receives the persisted invalidation (audience_changed|participant_revoked|conversation_access_revoked|message_deleted) with watermark, removedParticipants and reason; a sink throw rolls the acceptance and ledger back together; a pull ledger (invalidationsAfter) is also queryable
audienceModel.exposure: captureAudience returns metadata only (no summary/bodyRef/attachment refs); readContentRefs re-validates capture expiry, current audienceVersion, captured conversation, captured per-message revision and terminal state before returning content references; cross-audience/foreign message ids fail CROSS_AUDIENCE

watermarks.intakeSeq: one per persisted intake fact (accepted/stale/rejected/conflict); redeliveries return the original value
watermarks.invalidationWatermark: one per audience change / participant or conversation revocation / message deletion
watermarks.deletionWatermark: one per accepted retract/delete tombstone; deletion ledger rows keep message revision, native revision, kind, sourceEventId and reasonRef
watermarks.revocationWatermark: one per removed or explicitly revoked participant or revoked conversation
watermarks.queries: channel.watermark, channel.invalidationsAfter, channel.deletionsAfter, channel.revocationsAfter (monotonic, ordered, bounded 1..200)

integrationPoints.detail: the onInvalidation sink is synchronous and transactional; the test wires it to conversationRef -> conversationId mapping plus ConversationStore.invalidateAudience, proving stale drafts are retired and that a downstream throw rolls both stores back. Lead should add a ConversationDomain bridge method (invalidateAudience is currently private to ConversationStore usage inside ConversationDomain) and install the sink in worker.initialize once a persistent channelRef->conversationId mapping exists
channel.getParticipant().innerAccount feeds relationship.registerSubject; the same short id in two accounts produces two distinct entityIds while the same account tuple is idempotent

toConversationKey() emits the exact {connectionId, platformConversationId, threadId?, kind, scope} shape; the current single-owner deployment should pass scope `local-owner` and later multi-audience deployments need a scope per audience

LabDomain.ensureChannel expects {connectionId, runId, channelId, kind, membersDigest}; the ingress connectionId and audienceDigest(mode, participantRefs) can feed it without a second identity scheme. H6a does not open or modify Lab rooms

boundaries.note: All identities, channels, actors, messages and bodies are synthetic. No platform SDK, network call, native DSH Session, model, embedding, Lab room or device was used; no git commit/branch/reset was performed.

untested: No real platform adapter, credential, rate limit/reconnect semantics or provider edit/delete/read-receipt behavior (H6 activation requires separate scope).
No send/delivery path, Effect, draft generation or native Session binding (explicitly out of H6a; invalidation signal only).
ConversationDomain bridge method + worker sink installation is Lead integration; only the direct (same Worker) wiring is proven by test.
Dashboard/HTTP/UI projection of channel state is Lead/client scope and not implemented here.
Lab room reuse of channel identities is designed but not executed (no Lab room opened).

Long-run/throughput, disk-full/SIGKILL crash windows, migration/old-DB upgrade and multi-writer behavior are not measured; single-writer Worker plus WAL/DELETE selection stays inherited from the control store.
No long-lived OS/live-control-store evidence: all evidence comes from temporary synthetic SQLite files and a real Worker thread.

H6b: real platform adapter activation with explicit platform/account/payload/credential scope and delivery receipts.
Later: replyer/draft consumption of capture/readContentRefs, dashboard projection, Lab identity reuse, long-run and crash-window matrices.
